writeup.headline: UGA rates Buy on strong gasoline-futures gains and price momentum, with three factors lacking data.
writeup.thesis: United States Gasoline Fund is a commodity pool that tracks front-month RBOB gasoline futures, so its reported 'revenue' mostly reflects gains on those contracts rather than sales. The Buy rating and score of 70 rest on three factors: growth (75), trend (83) and news risk (50). Growth is strong on the reported figures, with TTM revenue growth of 717.3% and latest-quarter revenue growth of 64.1% year on year, though growth slowed by 2372.7 pp from the previous quarter. Trend is the strongest factor: the price is 31.0% above its 200-day average, shares are up 116.9% from 12 months ago to 1 month ago, and the price is 6.3% below its 52-week high. News was neutral across all topics, and quality, balance sheet and valuation did not contribute to the score.
key_risks: The fund's results and price move with gasoline futures, so a fall in RBOB prices would hit both reported growth and the trend score quickly.
Rolling front-month futures can cost money when later contracts trade above nearer ones, which can drag returns even if spot gasoline holds up.
Reported growth is very volatile for a futures fund, as shown by growth slowing by 2372.7 pp from the previous quarter.
Madison Dearborn Partners' pending purchase of Marygold, the parent of the general partner, depends on stockholder and regulatory approvals and could change how the sponsor is run.
Gasoline demand is seasonal, and a weaker winter period could weigh on prices after a run that left shares up 116.9% from 12 months ago to 1 month ago.
what_would_change: A drop of 6 points would take the score below 65 and the rating to Hold, most likely through a weaker trend score if gasoline futures fall back toward the 200-day average.
A gain of 10 points to 80 would lift the rating to Strong Buy, which would need stronger growth or trend readings or positive news.
A sharp reversal in futures gains would cut the growth score, which carries the largest weight at 0.4.
Negative news, such as problems with the sponsor's ownership change, would lower the news risk score from its neutral 50.
